analysis: Both changed files are test-only: NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift adds a TextSession fixture and nativeBlockRequestsCarryNoStopScope (head lines 50-71, 92-117), and the new ReasoningStopScopeTests.swift (head 1-82) covers stop-string scoping around reasoning and tool-call spans for the qwen3, deepseekR1, gemma4 and harmony parsers. No production code, wire format, key handling, attestation, cache storage or authorization path is modified here, so none of the threat model's assets (A-001, A-003, A-015/16, etc.) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011) change in this diff. The tests suggest the production PR changes stop-string matching semantics: reasoning and tool-call spans are excluded from stop matching, and the native block engine receives no scope and matches over the whole output. This is output-truncation behavior for consumer-visible text. It does not affect encryption, routing or attestation. It carries a minor correctness/availability implication (T-010, T-029 class) only if the production scope logic is wrong, and that logic is not in the supplied evidence (ReasoningStopScope, StopHoldback, CBv2StopStringScope, EngineV2Bridge.submitTokenized stopStringScope). Remaining uncertainty for integration: whether the production changes, in other batches, leak reasoning text to consumers or bypass stop limits so that generation runs to max_tokens, which would be a resource-consumption concern. Nothing in these test files establishes either. The T-041 prefix-cache mitigations are untouched; the new test sets cacheEnabled: false.
